title: docs: document navbar logo override and CSS sizing
description:
## Problem

The README documents per-product customizations for the navbar right-hand menu and the footer, but doesn't cover the navbar logo. This leaves two gaps:

1. Products don't know they can (and should) override the default `posit-icon-fullcolor.svg` with a product-specific mark via `website.navbar.logo` in their `_quarto.yml`.
2. The extension doesn't set a height for the navbar logo, so products need to add a CSS rule themselves — but there's no guidance on what that rule should be or where it goes.

This surfaced when investigating why the Connect docs footer looked different from Workbench after both were on the same theme version. The root cause was that the footer isn't bundled in the vendored extension (already documented), but separately it became clear the logo section was also missing.

## Proposed fix

Add a `#### Navbar logo` section to the README under `### Additional configuration entries`, between the existing `#### Navbar` and `#### Footer` sections.

title: Hidden cookie logic confuses a screenreader somewhat
description:
## Describe the bug
The cookie icon is not accessible via VoiceOver [when hidden](https://github.com/posit-dev/product-doc-theme/blob/main/_extensions/posit-docs/assets/_analytics.html#L18), which is great. However, since the logic that hides the cookie icon acts on the `<a>` that contains the icon and not on the containing `<li>` element, VoiceOver announces the list as having "5 items" when, in fact, only 4 are visible/accessible. We should tweak [the logic that determines what to hide](https://github.com/posit-dev/product-doc-theme/blob/main/_extensions/posit-docs/assets/_analytics.html#L13) to act instead on the containing `<li>`, which would make the "list of items" count be accurate.

### To reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. `quarto preview` any docs site using v7 of the theme
2. assuming you have a Mac, start VoiceOver
3. navigate to the footer
4. VoiceOver announces a list of "5 items" when in fact there are only four. (Or "four items" when there are only 3)

### Expected behavior
VoiceOver should announce the length of the list accurately

title: Always show Copy button in code blocks
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Follow-up from the PPM Quarto migration: https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C087T1PQSDR/p1739993749177159?thread_ts=1739405653.405299&cid=C087T1PQSDR

Copy buttons in Quarto code blocks are hidden and only visible over mouse hover by default. There is a config option to make Copy buttons always visible, and we think this would be useful to enable across the docs for usability and accessibility:

- Better discoverability of the Copy button for all users
- Better discoverability of the Copy button for keyboard-only users
- Somewhat mitigates a bug with Copy buttons not appearing on keyboard focus (https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/12118)
- Keeps consistency with the previous MkDocs Material site always showing Copy buttons
- https://quarto.org/ has also enabled Copy buttons always showing by default

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I'm not sure where this would be added, but the config option is at: https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-code.html#copy-button
```yaml
format:
  html:
    code-copy: true
```

[Learn how aria-hidden affects focusable elements](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.8/aria-hidden-focus). **Uncategorized - unsure if we can fix** - [ ] [aria-hidden="true"] elements contain focusable descendants **(Quarto team thinks that this is[ resolved in v1.5](https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C01LQETLA7L/p1714583175668939?thread_ts=1714580460.240939&cid=C01LQETLA7L) so I can verify at a later date - however, the Quarto website doesn't have this issue so I am assuming that v1.5 does in fact resolve this issue)** >Focusable descendents within an [aria-hidden="true"] element prevent those interactive elements from being available to users of assistive technologies like screen readers. description: One you install the extension, there are several additional/manual steps that one must take to add things like: - favicon - header/nav entries - footer - link external icon - link external new window - toc: true - etc. See example below: ``` website: title: favicon: "assets/images/favicon.svg" bread-crumbs: true navbar: pinned: true logo: "images/posit-icon-fullcolor.svg" logo-alt: "Posit documentation" sidebar: style: "floating" collapse-level: 1 search: true pinned: false page-footer: left: - text: © 2024 Posit Software, PBC formerly RStudio, PBC url: "https://posit.co/" center: | Posit Product 12345 right: - icon: book href: https://docs.posit.co/ - icon: question-circle-fill href: https://support.posit.co/hc/en-us - icon: lightbulb-fill href: https://solutions.posit.co/ format: html: theme: - _extensions/posit-dev/posittheme/theme.scss link-external-icon: true link-external-newwindow: true toc: true toc-expand: true ``` I am manually sending this block to people vs. some of these entries being applied automatically. This kind of "undoes" some of the efficiency of having a "default theme". @edavidaja had mentioned: >_extensions subdirectory for the theme, it could be set up so that ```format: posit-docs-html: default ``` Looking for ways to improve this and remove some of the manual steps that need to be taken to align the sites.

title: Repoint navbar "Posit Support" link to the ticket form (SUP-722)
description:
As part of [SUP-722](https://positpbc.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-722) / rstudio/docs.rstudio.com#2761, Support is consolidating ticket-submission guidance and the Zendesk KB articles on support.posit.co are being retired. support.posit.co is becoming primarily a place to submit a ticket and sign in, rather than an article library.

The shared theme navbar **Help** dropdown includes a **Posit Support** item that currently points at the Help Center landing (which is being gutted). It should point directly at the ticket-submission form to match the site's new purpose.

## Change

In `_extensions/posit-docs/_extension.yml` (navbar Help menu):

```yaml
- text: Posit Support
  href: https://support.posit.co/hc/en-us/   # -> https://support.posit.co/hc/en-us/requests/new
```

This mirrors the corresponding change to the navbar **Help** link in docs.rstudio.com (rstudio/docs.rstudio.com#2761).

## Also check

- `example/_quarto.yml` has a footer **Support** link to `https://support.posit.co/hc/en-us` that may warrant the same update for consistency.

Because this theme is versioned and consumed by all product docs sites, the change will need a theme release and downstream bumps.
